races.title: State Senate, District 14
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Esmeralda Soria
cands.bio: Democrat and member of the California State Assembly for District 27 since December 2022. Fresno City Council member 2015–2022. Former policy aide, district director to a state senator, and policy advisor to an assemblymember. Adjunct professor at Fresno City College. UC Berkeley graduate with a UC Davis law degree.

endorsements.text: 2026 State Senate endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include the Democratic Party of California, California Federation of Labor Unions, California Teachers Association, IUOE Local 3, SEIU Local 521, California Young Democrats and Equality California.

cands.gaps: We could not find documented actions or bill details from her time in office on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, growth limits, police pay, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. We found no current statements from her on those topics either. Her gun and immigration positions come from a 2020 congressional campaign, not her current race. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2020, 2022, 2024 or 2026. Ballotpedia's list of bills she sponsored did not load, so we could not review them.

local.label: Roots 100: Wikipedia says she was born and raised in Visalia to immigrant parents from Michoacán, Mexico, and her campaign site says she was raised in Tulare County and is a lifelong Central Valley resident.

qual.background: Assembly member since 2022 and Fresno City Council member 2015–2022 (council president). She holds a law degree and worked as a Capitol policy aide, a legal-aid foundation project director, a state senator's district director and a policy advisor to an assemblymember.

second-amendment.evidence: On her 2020 congressional campaign website she proposed banning the sale of assault weapons, limiting magazine capacity, closing the "Charleston Loophole," running buy-back programs and enforcing strict universal background checks.

workers-first.evidence: On her 2020 congressional campaign website she said she supports comprehensive immigration reform with a path to citizenship for people already in the country, and criticized the detention of asylum seekers.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: On her 2020 congressional campaign website she said California needs four million new housing units and that "to solve our housing crisis, we need more housing," calling for cutting red tape. She said she worked with developers to bring hundreds of new housing units to Fresno.

cands.name: Darin S. DuPont
cands.bio: Republican candidate for California State Senate District 14 in the Central Valley. He advanced from the June 2, 2026 nonpartisan primary with 40.4% of the vote and faced Democrat Esmeralda Soria in the November general election. His campaign focuses on affordability, water security and government accountability.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists Reform California among his endorsements and voter-guide recommendations. It also lists several social-media voter guides and a radio program, The Morning Answer with Jennifer Horn.

cands.gaps: We could not find his birthplace, where he grew up, when he moved to California, or his career and any past offices, so his background and California ties are not rated. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey. His campaign site lists only broad priorities (affordability for young families, water storage and infrastructure, and transparency and ending one-party control), with no specific proposals. We found nothing on his positions on data centers, development, property taxes, immigration, guns, abortion, policing or schools. We found no documented actions in office, controversies or foreign ties.
